newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends steady to higher, off highs.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends steady to higher, off highs.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled higher in active dealings on fund and commercial buying, but late weakness in outside markets pushed spring wheat off its intraday highs, traders said.
Traders said early commercial buying may have been tied to the Canadian Wheat Board's rumored sale of wheat to Algeria.

"We've got somebody out of Canada that came in and bought several million bushels," a trader said, adding that the Canadian buyer had likely cleared through Linnco Futures. Traders said Linnco bought a total of three million September bushels and 2.5 million December bushels Wednesday.

The commercial buying ushered in some fund-related buying, and traders said they also noted commercial buying at the close. One trader speculated this was connected to Taiwan's upcoming tender for 99,000 tonnes of wheat.
MGE spring wheat settled unchanged to five cents per bushel higher, with Sept up five cents at $3.91-3/4.
Wednesday's volume was estimated at 30.439 million bushels, up from Tuesday's volume of 25.435 million.

Apart from Linnco, other featured players were Prudential, which sold two million Sept. Country Hedging sold 2.6 million Sept. Continental, Cargill Investor Services and Benson-Quinn each bought at least 1.5 million Sept.
